summary: Abanindranath Tagore worked in history, archaeology, and other fields. He studied at Sanskrit Collegiate School, Sanskrit College and University, and the Government College of Art & Craft (~1890–1894), later holding a post at the University of Calcutta (~1921–1929).

Abdur Rehman is an Indologist and archaeologist who earned his PhD at the Australian National University under Arthur Llewellyn Basham and studied under Ahmad Hasan Dani. In 1988, he was an assistant professor of archaeology at the University of Peshawar.

Abel Bergaigne was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Michel Bréal and Eugène-Louis Hauvette-Besnault (~1867–1869). He taught at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1869–1888), Sorbonne University (lecturer in 1877, professor in 1885), and University of Paris (~1877–1888).

Abigail I. MacBain works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She earned her MA at McMaster University, studying under Mark Rowe, James A. Benn, Shayne Clarke, Mark MacWilliams, and Michael Greenwald, and is attested at the University of Edinburgh in 2026.

Abraham Hyacinthe Anquetil-Duperron worked in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and religious studies. He studied at Sorbonne University, Old Catholic Seminary of Amersfoort, and under Dastur Darab, holding posts at the Bibliothèque nationale de France and the Institut de France.

Abraham Sachs worked in history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at Johns Hopkins University (~1934–1939) and held posts at the Institute for Advanced Study in 1945 and Brown University from circa 1948 to 1983.

Abraham Valentine Williams Jackson worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at Columbia University and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg under Edward Washburn Hopkins, later serving as fellow and professor at Columbia (1883–1935).
Abraham Zablocki specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Cornell University and held a post attested in 2008 at Agnes Scott College.

Achim Bayer specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen, worked as a research associate at the University of Munich (2004–2006), and was a research fellow at Hamburg in 2026.

Adalbert Bezzenberger was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Theodor Benfey at the University of Göttingen and at the University of Munich. He held posts at Göttingen (1874) and the University of Königsberg (1879–1921), serving as rector.

Adalbert Kuhn, an Indologist and linguist, completed his promotion at Humboldt University of Berlin (1833–1837) under Franz Bopp. He served as a teacher, professor, and director at Köllnisches Gymnasium between 1837 and 1870.

Adam Bowles is an Indologist and scholar of religious studies who completed his doctoral studies under Greg Bailey. He served as a senior lecturer in Asian Religions at the University of Queensland, attested from 2016 to 2018.

Adam Hardy is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Trinity College, Cambridge, served as Director at De Montfort University (~1994–2002), and became Professor of Asian Architecture at Cardiff University around 2002.

Adam Pearcey specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at SOAS University of London under Ulrich Pagel, Nathan W. Hill, and Vincent Tournier, having also studied under numerous traditional Tibetan teachers.

Adam Yuet Chau specializes in Sinology and religious studies. He studied at Williams College and Stanford University (PhD 2001), held a postdoctoral fellowship at Harvard University, and served as lecturer and professor of anthropology at the University of Cambridge.

Adelheid Herrmann-Pfandt specializes in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Erlangen-Nuremberg, Bonn, and Marburg, and held posts as a visiting professor at the University of Vienna (2005) and Privatdozentin at the University of Marburg (2009).

Adelheid Mette was an Indologist who completed her promotion and habilitation at the University of Hamburg. She served as a professor at the University of Münster (1971; 1988–2000) and held professorial positions at the University of Munich (1978, 1980, 2000).

Aden Kumler is an art historian who studied at the University of Chicago, University of Toronto, and Harvard University. She was an assistant professor at the University of Chicago (2007) and became a professor at the University of Basel in 2020.
Adeu Rinpoche was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teachers Khamtrul Rinpoche, Samten Gyatso, and Chögon Rinpoche, and taught Tsoknyi Rinpoche.

Adhémard Leclère worked in religious studies, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He served as Résident de France at Kratié in the French Protectorate of Cambodia and as vice-president of the Société Ethnologique de Paris, which he founded.
